text: The accounting equation is stated as:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Assets = Liabilities + Capital|Assets + Capital = Liabilities|Capital = Assets + Liabilities|Assets = Capital - Liabilities
explanation: Assets equal the sum of outside claims (liabilities) and the owner's claims (capital).

text: Recording a transaction in the journal for the first time is called:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Posting|Journalising|Ledgerising|Balancing off
explanation: The journal is the book of original entry.

text: When cash is received from a customer on account the entry is:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Debit Cash and Credit Sales|Debit Sales and Credit Cash|Debit Cash and Credit the customer's account|Debit the customer's account and Credit Cash
explanation: Cash (asset) increases with a debit and the debtor's claim decreases with a credit.

text: Every transaction affects at least two accounts in equal amounts. This is the:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: This is the dual aspect concept of double entry book keeping.

text: State the dual aspect concept of accounting.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Every transaction has two equal and opposite effects so two entries (a debit and a credit) are recorded.

text: The ledger is called the book of:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Original entry|Final entry|Subsidiary entry only|Cash entry
explanation: The journal records transactions first and the ledger (final entry) groups them by account.

text: The trial balance is prepared mainly to check the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Profitability of the business|Arithmetic accuracy of ledger posting|Solvency of the business|Efficiency of the staff
explanation: Equality of total debits and credits detects one sided and amount errors.

text: A cash account showing a credit balance in the trial balance indicates:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: A cash shortage|An overdrawn position|A credit sale|An arithmetical error only
explanation: When the bank pays more than the business deposits the cash book balance becomes negative.

text: The trial balance will NOT detect an error of omission. This statement is:
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: When a transaction is completely left out both sides stay equal so the trial balance agrees.

text: List any four errors that are not disclosed by the trial balance.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Errors of omission; errors of commission; errors of principle; and compensating errors.

text: The statement that shows the profit earned from trading is the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Profit and Loss Account|Trading Account|Balance Sheet|Cash Flow Statement
explanation: The trading account computes gross profit from sales and cost of goods sold.

text: Gross profit is calculated as:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Net sales minus all expenses|Net sales minus cost of goods sold|Revenue plus capital|Sales minus drawings
explanation: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases + direct expenses - closing stock.

text: Closing stock is shown:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Only in the Balance Sheet|Only in the Trading Account|On the credit side of the Trading Account and as current asset in the Balance Sheet|Only in the Profit and Loss Account
explanation: It is valued for the trading account and reported as a current asset.

text: A current liability such as a creditor is shown on the:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Assets side of the Balance Sheet|Liabilities side of the Balance Sheet|Debit side of the Trading Account|Credit side of the P and L Account only
explanation: Liabilities and capital appear on the liabilities side of the balance sheet.

text: Distinguish between gross profit and net profit.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Gross profit is sales minus cost of goods sold; net profit is gross profit minus operating expenses plus non operating incomes.

text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to reconcile:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: The cash book balance with the pass book balance|The trial balance with the balance sheet|Sales with debtors|Assets with liabilities
explanation: It explains differences such as cheques not presented and bank charges not recorded.

text: A cheque deposited and recorded in the cash book but not yet cleared by the bank is in the BRS:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Deducted from the pass book balance|Added to the pass book balance|Ignored completely|Debited in the pass book
explanation: The pass book has not yet received the credit so it is added to reach the cash book figure.

text: Depreciation is charged because of:
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Physical wear and tear only|Obsolescence only|The passage of time; wear and tear; and obsolescence|Capital loss only
explanation: The service potential of a fixed asset falls for all three reasons.

text: Under the straight line method the depreciation charge each year is the same on the original cost.
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: A fixed percentage of the original cost is charged until the asset is fully depreciated.

text: State any three methods of providing depreciation.
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Straight line method; diminishing balance method; and units of production method.

text: A valid contract requires:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Offer and acceptance only|Free consent; lawful consideration; competent parties; and a lawful object|A written document only|Stamp paper only
explanation: All the essentials under the Indian Contract Act 1872 must be present together.

text: An agreement without consideration is generally:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Always valid|Void|Enforceable by the court|A quasi contract
explanation: Consideration is a price in legal terms and agreement without it is void except narrow exceptions.

text: Coercion in the Indian Contract Act means:
subject: Commercial Law
options: An expression of two or more meanings|Obtaining consent by unlawful pressure or threat|A casual promise|A written notice
explanation: Coercion vitiates free consent and makes the contract voidable.

text: A contract may come to an end by performance; mutual agreement; or lapse of time. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: These are the standard modes of discharge of a contract.

text: List the essentials of a valid contract under the Indian Contract Act.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Offer and acceptance; intention to create legal relation; competent parties; free consent; lawful consideration; lawful object; and it must not be declared void.

text: In the absence of a special agreement risk normally follows:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Delivery|Title|Payment|The invoice date
explanation: Where property passes the loss by destruction falls on the owner even before delivery.

text: A sale of goods is complete when:
subject: Commercial Law
options: The full price is paid|Property in the goods passes from the seller to the buyer|The goods reach the buyer|The invoice is issued
explanation: Transfer of property is the defining moment of sale.

text: Goods under the Sale of Goods Act include:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Money only|All movable property other than money and actionable claims|Land and buildings|Shares in a company
explanation: The Act covers movables such as stock and growing crops but not money or intangible claims.

text: In a sale on approval the buyer may test the goods and return them if not satisfied. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: Property passes only when the buyer approves or keeps the goods beyond the allowed time.

text: State the conditions implied under the Sale of Goods Act.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Seller's title; merchantable quality; fitness for the particular purpose; and correspondence with description.

text: A cheque is a negotiable instrument under:
subject: Commercial Law
options: The Indian Contract Act|The Negotiable Instruments Act|The Sales Tax Act|The Companies Act
explanation: The Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 governs promissory notes; bills of exchange; and cheques.

text: A bill of exchange is a written instruction:
subject: Commercial Law
options: From the drawer to the drawee to pay a certain sum to the order of a person|From the buyer to the seller|From the bank to the customer only|From the government to the citizen
explanation: It involves three parties: the drawer; the drawee; and the payee.

text: A holder in due course must take the instrument:
subject: Commercial Law
options: After maturity only|In good faith and for value before or at maturity|By gift only|From a stranger to the chain
explanation: These conditions give the holder a better title than the transferor.

text: A promissory note is made and signed by the debtor who promises to pay. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: The maker of a note is the principal debtor and only two parties are involved.

text: Distinguish between a promissory note and a bill of exchange.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: A note is a written promise by the maker to pay and has two parties; a bill is a written order from drawer to drawee and has three parties; a note needs no acceptance.

text: The Consumer Protection Act 2019 replaced the:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Act of 1986|Contract Act of 1872|Sale of Goods Act of 1930|Companies Act of 2013
explanation: The 2019 Act introduced e commerce protection and a three level commission structure.

text: A dissatisfied consumer may approach the:
subject: Commercial Law
options: Supreme Court only|Appropriate Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission|Police station only|A private arbitration tribunal only
explanation: Complaints go to the district; state; or national commission depending on the value of the claim.

text: Deficiency in service means any fault or lack in the quality or standard of service. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: It covers poor quality; delay; and non performance of promised services.

text: The basic consumer rights include the right to safety; information; choice; and redressal. This statement is:
subject: Commercial Law
explanation: The Act also lists the right to be heard and consumer education.

text: List any four rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act.
subject: Commercial Law
correctAnswer: Right to safety; right to be informed; right to choose; right to redressal; right to be heard; and consumer education.

text: The probability of an impossible event is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: An impossible event never occurs so its probability is zero.

text: The sum of the probabilities of all outcomes of a random experiment is:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: 0|1|Greater than 1|Undefined
explanation: All possible outcomes together are certain so their probabilities add to one.

text: The standard deviation is the square root of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Range|Variance|Median|Mode
explanation: It expresses the average spread of data around the mean in the original units.

text: The mean of a grouped frequency distribution can be estimated by the step deviation method. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: It is a shortcut of the assumed mean method that works on small coded deviations.

text: State Bayes theorem in words.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: The posterior probability of a cause given observed evidence equals the prior probability of the cause times the likelihood of the evidence divided by the total probability of the evidence.

text: An index number expresses the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Absolute change in a single item|Relative change in a group of related variables|Only a single price|Quantity of goods produced
explanation: It measures percentage change of a group of prices; quantities; or values against a base period.

text: The simple aggregate method of constructing a price index is also called the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Geometric method|Arithmetic method|Weighted method|Fisher method
explanation: It divides the aggregate of current prices by the aggregate of base prices and multiplies by 100.

text: Fishers ideal index number is the geometric mean of the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Laspeyres and Paasche indices|Base year and current year prices|Quantity index and price index|Two aggregate indices
explanation: It satisfies the time reversal and factor reversal tests.

text: A consumer price index is mainly useful for measuring household inflation. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: It tracks price changes of a fixed basket of consumer goods and services.

text: State any four uses of index numbers.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: Measuring inflation; deflating values into real terms; comparing changes over time and across regions; and guiding economic policy.

text: The four components of a time series are:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Trend; seasonal; cyclical; and irregular|Mean; median; mode; and range|Debit; credit; balance; and total|Input; output; stock; and flow
explanation: Any observed value is modeled as a combination of these four forces.

text: The long term rising or falling movement in data is called the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Seasonal variation|Trend|Irregular variation|Business cycle
explanation: It is the secular movement that shows the general direction of the series.

text: Seasonal variation is a change within a year that repeats regularly. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: Examples are holiday shopping peaks and monsoon demand patterns.

text: The moving average method is used to estimate the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Trend|Mode|Irregular variation only|Random error only
explanation: Averaging over a window smooths seasonal and irregular fluctuations to reveal the trend.

text: Explain the concept of the business cycle.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: It is the recurring but irregular rise and fall of economic activity around the trend with the phases of prosperity; recession; depression; and recovery.

text: In a linear programming problem the objective is to:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Maximize or minimize a linear function subject to linear constraints|Solve a quadratic equation|Compute a determinant|Balance the books of account
explanation: Both the objective function and the constraints must be linear.

text: The set of all feasible solutions of a linear programming problem is called the:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Objective region|Feasible region|Shadow region|Dual region
explanation: It is the common area satisfying every constraint including non negativity.

text: The simplex method moves from one:
subject: Business Mathematics
options: Random point to another random point|Corner point to an adjacent better corner point|Center to the edge of the graph|Row to the next column
explanation: An optimum of a linear program always lies at a vertex of the feasible region.

text: Slack variables are added to less than or equal to constraints to convert them into equations. This statement is:
subject: Business Mathematics
explanation: They represent the unused portion of a scarce resource.

text: State the steps of the graphical method for a two variable linear programming problem.
subject: Business Mathematics
correctAnswer: Plot each constraint line; shade the feasible region; evaluate the objective function at every corner point; and choose the corner that gives the best value.

text: According to the law of demand a rise in price causes the quantity demanded to fall. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: The inverse relation holds when other determinants remain unchanged (ceteris paribus).

text: A shift of the demand curve (not a movement along it) is caused by:
subject: Economics
options: A change in the own price of the good|A change in consumer income|A change in the quantity demanded|A change in the price alone
explanation: Income; tastes; prices of related goods; expectations; and the number of buyers shift the curve.

text: When demand rises and supply stays the same the equilibrium price:
subject: Economics
options: Falls|Rises|Stays the same|Becomes zero
explanation: The demand curve shifts right and the intersection moves up along the supply curve.

text: Perfectly elastic demand has a price elasticity of:
subject: Economics
options: 0|1|Infinity|-1
explanation: Any rise in price makes quantity demanded drop to zero.

text: Distinguish between a movement along the demand curve and a shift of the demand curve.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: A movement along the curve is caused only by a change in the own price; a shift is caused by changes in income; tastes; prices of related goods; expectations; or the number of buyers.

text: The income method of computing national income adds up:
subject: Economics
options: The factor incomes of all producers|Final consumer spending|Exports only|Government debt
explanation: Wages; rent; interest; and profit are summed to get factor income at factor cost.

text: GNP at market prices equals GDP at factor cost plus net factor income from abroad plus:
subject: Economics
options: Indirect taxes minus subsidies|Subsidies minus indirect taxes|Depreciation|Interest on debt
explanation: Statistical adjustments convert factor cost into market prices.

text: Per capita income is national income divided by the population. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: It is used to compare the average income and living standard across countries.

text: The output method computes national income as the sum of value added at each stage of production. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: Adding value added avoids double counting of intermediate goods.

text: List three problems in the measurement of national income.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Double counting; non monetary transactions such as home work; and the underground economy of unrecorded activity.

text: The functions of money include:
subject: Economics
options: Medium of exchange; store of value; and unit of account|Only lending|Only payment of taxes|Only savings
explanation: These three are the classic functions recognized in monetary theory.

text: The central bank of India is the:
subject: Economics
options: State Bank of India|Reserve Bank of India|National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development|Union Bank of India
explanation: The RBI acts as banker to the government and to commercial banks.

text: The cash reserve ratio is the fraction of deposits that banks must keep with the RBI as cash. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: Raising the CRR reduces the money banks can lend and tightens liquidity.

text: An increase in the repo rate usually:
subject: Economics
options: Increases the money supply|Reduces the money supply and helps curb inflation|Raises inflation directly|Increases the cash reserve ratio automatically
explanation: Borrowing becomes costlier so credit growth slows and demand pressure eases.

text: Explain the credit creation function of commercial banks.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Banks lend out a portion of deposits; when the loan amount is redeposited it is lent again; the process multiplies the initial deposit by the money multiplier which equals one divided by the cash reserve ratio.

text: A country has a comparative advantage when it can produce a good at a:
subject: Economics
options: Higher absolute cost|Lower opportunity cost|Zero cost|Equal cost to others
explanation: Gains from trade arise from differences in opportunity costs not absolute costs.

text: The main advantage of free trade is:
subject: Economics
options: Protection of infant industries|Efficient allocation of resources and higher consumer welfare|Higher tariffs on imports|Reduced competition
explanation: Resources move to their most productive use and consumers get variety at lower prices.

text: The balance of payments is in equilibrium when the current account plus the capital account equals zero. This statement is:
subject: Economics
explanation: A deficit in one account is financed by a surplus in the other.

text: A depreciation of the rupee makes:
subject: Economics
options: Indian exports cheaper for foreign buyers|Imports cheaper for Indians|Both exports and imports cheaper|International trade impossible
explanation: Foreign buyers need fewer of their own currency units for the same rupee price.

text: Distinguish between free trade and protectionism.
subject: Economics
correctAnswer: Free trade removes barriers such as tariffs and quotas so goods move freely; protectionism keeps those barriers to shield domestic industries at the cost of efficiency and higher consumer prices.
